tools.name: scene_update
tools.description: Edit a scene card. The change is saved on the timeline scene and appears in the open Video Builder. Only the keys sent change; an empty string, false or [] clears or disables a field. Read the current card with scene_get (scene_card). Notes: timeline_note (Director Notes), i2v_notes (Video Notes), notes (Planning Notes), prompt_summary. Lyrics: lyric_text, lyric_section, lyric_singers, lyric_cue_map, lyric_no_lip_sync, lyric_instrumental, lyric_performance_mode, lyric_shot_word_timing_enabled, speaker_assignments. Camera and character: shot_type, camera_motion, character_motion, no_character_present. Performance: performance_mode (singing|speaking|no_lip_sync), performance_style, facial_performance, facial_performance_custom, include_microphone. Audio and continuity: audio_direction, continuity, flf_start_state, flf_transformation, flf_end_state, flf_carry_forward. Look: video_style, video_style_custom, temporal_world_effect_override, temporal_world_effect_custom, trigger_phrase, trigger_position. References: subject_ids (list of character ids), location_id. Prompts: image_prompt, video_prompt, video_prompt_origin, minimax_h3_pass2_prompt, plus the single prompt fields and timing. Timed Timeline Notes are separate: use timeline_note_create.

tools.name: stitch_final
tools.description: Stitch rendered scene videos into FINAL_VIDEO.mp4. When the project has overlays (GET /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers), the stitch draws them onto the video and the job result has an `overlay_layers` section (applied, clips, skipped). Send `overlay_layers: false` to leave them out. The project's transitions (GET /projects/{pid}/transitions) are drawn on the video where their blocks lie, and the job result has `transitions` and `transition_notes` when there are any. Send `transitions` (a list of {transition, start, seconds, params}, start on the timeline in seconds) to use other ones for this stitch. The project's filters (GET /projects/{pid}/filters) and effects (GET /projects/{pid}/effects) are drawn on the joined video after the transitions, filters first, and the job result has `looks` and `look_notes` when there are any. Send `filters` or `effects` (a list of {look, start, seconds, intensity, params}) to use other ones for this stitch.

tools.name: timeline_from_lines
tools.description: Create the timeline scenes from the project's lyrics, like Line Mapping in the Builder. Times the lyrics (or reuses a saved timing), makes one scene per lyric line, fills instrumental gaps, then merges scenes shorter than min_scene_seconds and cuts scenes longer than max_scene_seconds. Runs as a job (use job_wait). Refuses to replace existing scenes unless replace_existing is true, and never replaces scenes that already have images or videos.

enforce_lengths.description: False keeps one scene per lyric line whatever its length

use_saved_alignment.description: Reuse the timing from lyrics_align instead of running it again

tools.name: timeline_enforce_length
tools.description: Merge scenes shorter than min_scene_seconds and cut scenes longer than max_scene_seconds. A 12 s scene becomes two 6 s scenes with its lyrics divided; short scenes merge into the neighbor that gives the shorter result. Uses the safe merge/split edits that keep image and video numbering correct. Scenes with rendered video are left alone and listed. Use dry_run to preview.

tools.name: story_create
tools.description: Write a story layer step with the project's LLM, as a background job. step 'arc' writes the story arc from the story idea, 'brief' writes the song story brief, 'beats' writes a beat per scene (only scenes without one unless replace_existing; limit caps the count). Returns a job id for job_wait. Order: arc, brief, beats. Story Mode (video_type 'story') uses its own steps: 'book' writes the story book from story_idea, 'split' turns a story you pass as text into chapters without changing a word, 'convert' does the same with an older project's story arc, 'chapter' rewrites chapter_id following direction, 'cast' lists story characters that have no card (nothing saved), 'remove_people' rewrites the book without the people in names, 'acts' splits every chapter (or chapter_id) into acts, 'plan' gives every scene (or act_id's scenes) a story slice, spot, mood and performance, 'locations' makes a location card per place and maps the scenes (from the story, never the lyrics): before the plan it finds the places inside each chapter setting (the Places tab), and with map_only after the plan it only maps each scene to a card that exists. For LM Studio the loaded model is used and never changed.

style_theme.description: locations only: look and banned places.

map_only.description: locations only: after the plan, map each scene to a location card that exists and make nothing (no LLM).

regenerate_looks.description: locations only: write every setting's look again.

replace_descriptions.description: locations only: replace the description of a card that has one.

act_id.description: plan only: rebuild one act's scenes.

spot_min_scenes.description: plan only: fewest scenes in a row at one spot.

story_idea.description: arc and book; defaults to the saved idea.

tone_notes.description: book only: tone, genre and world notes.

text.description: split only: the full story to divide into chapters.

names.description: remove_people only: who to write out.

Fields are saved on the timeline scene with the Builder's keys, and the open Video Builder shows the change (fields marked card only belong to a Storyboard card, which this app does not have): `timeline_note` (Director Notes; alias `director_note`), `i2v_notes` (Video Notes; saved as `motion_summary` on the card; aliases `video_notes`, `motion_summary`), `notes` (Planning Notes), `prompt_summary` (card only), `label`, `lyric_text` (alias `lyrics`; sets `lyric_no_lip_sync` from the text unless you send it), `lyric_section`, `story_beat`, `lyric_singers`, `lyric_cue_map`, `lyric_no_lip_sync`, `lyric_instrumental`, `lyric_performance_mode`, `lyric_shot_word_timing_enabled`, `speaker_assignments`, `shot_type`, `camera_motion`, `character_motion`, `no_character_present`, `performance_mode` (`singing`, `speaking`, `no_lip_sync`), `performance_style`, `facial_performance`, `facial_performance_custom`, `emotion_expression_tags` (up to 1200 characters; scene mood/expression direction interpreted by the LLM), `include_microphone`, `audio_direction`, `continuity`, `flf_start_state`, `flf_transformation`, `flf_end_state`, `flf_carry_forward`, `video_style`, `video_style_custom`, `temporal_world_effect_override`, `temporal_world_effect_custom`, `trigger_phrase`, `trigger_position` (card only), `video_prompt_type`, `subject_ids` (the scene's characters) and `location_id` (the Reference Builder scene maps), `image_prompt` and `video_prompt` (written like a Builder prompt edit for the project's image model and video engine; `video_prompt_origin`), `minimax_h3_pass2_prompt`. Also the single fields `t2i_prompt`, `i2v_prompt`, `enhance_prompt`, `minimax_h3_prompt`, `flux_prompt`, `nb_prompt`, `flow_gpt_prompt`, `ernie_t2i_prompt`, `minimax_h3_i2v_frame_mode` (`normal` or `flf`, per scene), `first_last_frame_end_image_path` (explicit last image for I2V FLF), `minimax_h3_continuation_direction` (what a scene continued with `latent_continuation_masked` does after its first moments, one smooth movement, no cut), `minimax_h3_continuation_start_seconds` (second of that scene where the direction starts: 0.5 by default, at most half the scene, `null` resets), `start`, `end`, or per-scene `use_scene_*` / `*_settings`. `use_scene_minimax_h3_settings` must be a boolean, and `minimax_h3_settings` is checked against GET /settings/minimax-h3/schema (for example `sage_attention`, `use_memory_efficient_sage_attention`, `use_block_sparse_attention`, `two_pass_use_block_sparse_attention`, `pass1_use_block_sparse_attention`, `pass2_use_block_sparse_attention`) and merged into the scene's saved settings; an invalid value returns 400 and nothing is saved. Only the keys sent change; an empty string, `false`, `0` or `[]` is saved as sent, so a field can be cleared or turned off. A field that cannot be patched returns a validation error that lists the supported fields, and nothing is saved. `storyboard_card` in the reply lists the Storyboard card fields that changed. The scene_defaults object stores per-scene Scene Defaults under the project setting names (camera_flow, camera_motion_speed, character_motion_speed, minimax_h3_cut_frequency, minimax_h3_cut_style, performance/facial fields and visual options); false, zero and empty values are explicit overrides. Story arc detail stays project-wide. Nonempty scene_defaults objects merge existing overrides; an empty object clears that record.

Speaking mode only: read scene overrides, effective/project settings, scene-owned dialogue clips, audio span, padded total duration, current scene duration, needs_render and the scene_dialogue editor draft. Uses the scene ID, not its position.

Speaking mode only: patch `settings` (`use_project_defaults`, `fit_duration`: booleans; `silence_before`, `silence_after`: 0–60 seconds). Optionally import base64/data-URL `audio_data` with `audio_name`, or remove owned dialogue with `clear_audio: true`. Also accepts a `dialogue` draft (speaker_id, text, delivery, allow_rewrite, model_id) saved on that scene as scene_dialogue. Generated audio and API keys are never stored in the draft. Fits duration to dialogue plus silence and ripples later scenes and attached audio; independent tracks stay fixed. Originals are preserved. Supports If-Match; frozen timelines and running scene renders reject edits.

Speaking only: create an LLM job using the saved runner, assigned character voice and elevenlabs_dialogue instruction preset. Optional dialogue object overrides the saved scene draft: speaker_id, text, delivery, allow_rewrite (default false), model_id (eleven_v4 default or eleven_v3). Returns editable tagged text; preserves spoken words unless rewriting is explicitly allowed. Does not call ElevenLabs or save the draft. Wait for the returned job ID.

Speaking only: explicitly generate one MP3 take with the saved ElevenLabs key and the chosen character's enabled voice. Optional dialogue overrides the saved scene_dialogue draft. Returns audio_data (MP3 data URL), audio_name, voice_id and dialogue. Uses credits; never retries automatically and does not write project state. Preview, then import via PATCH audio-settings with audio_data, audio_name, dialogue and If-Match to fit/ripple the scene. The project's own key is used; without one, the key saved in H3 Studio's App Settings.
Merge a scene with its neighbour (`with_direction`: previous or next). Lyrics are joined.

What the Video Builder's Choose MiniMax References button shows for a scene: `available` (every character, extra, location and ingredients sheet with an image, each with its `key`, whether the scene mapping already picks it, and its `image_number` when selected), `selected` (the order sent to MiniMax), `custom` (chosen by hand or following the scene mappings), `automatic_keys` and the `limits` (`max_choices` is 8: a scene sends at most 8 references, and the scene image used as Image 1 is a ninth image) and `over_limit_by` (how many mapped references the render leaves out). `pipeline` says which view you got: `standard` (the view above) or, when the MiniMax H3 project renders with RefMods, `refmod`: `items` in render order, each with its prompt `label` (`<Video N>`, `<Picture N>`, `<Audio N>`), card, `category`, `reference_type` (props included), `strength`, `tokens` and `source` (`refmod` name, `found`, `kind`, `frames`, `canvas`, read from the RefMod file like the render), `labels`, `tokens` (`total`, `limit`, `over_limit`, `imbalance`), `warnings` and `editable: false`.

Choose the ordered MiniMax references for a scene: `keys` is the list from `available` (for example `["subject:ava", "location:roof", "location:alley"]`, several locations are allowed), or `automatic: true` to follow the scene mappings again. Unknown or repeated keys and too many keys are refused with the allowed keys listed. In a RefMod project the render ignores this order, so the call returns 422 NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_MODE and saves nothing; change the scene's references with PUT /references/scene-mapping instead. _(If-Match)_
Move a scene to `start_time`. `ripple` shifts the others.

The context brief an outside agent needs to write a prompt itself: cast, cut plan and character budget (`kind`). A scene continued with `latent_continuation_masked` also gets a `continuation` block: `hold_seconds`, the scene's `direction` and the `rules` for writing it as the next moment of the previous scene's take.
Rewrite an existing scene prompt following an instruction.
Improve an existing scene prompt with the LLM.
Write one scene's image prompt with the LLM, from the scene's notes, lyric and references (`user_notes` overrides them).
Build a MiniMax prompt from shot descriptions you provide (`shots`, `mode`). `save` stores it. A reference-to-video prompt gets the same subject definitions and soundscape as `minimax-prompts`.
Check a MiniMax prompt against the length and format rules.
Write one scene's video prompt with the LLM (`mode`), from its image prompt, motion notes and references.
Set a prompt field directly (`t2i_prompt`, `i2v_prompt`, `minimax_h3_prompt`, ...). Body: `prompt`, `origin`.
Change a scene's length (`duration` or `end_time`). `ripple` shifts the others.
Split a scene at `at_time`. `clear_right_media` drops the media on the new right half. Lyrics follow their words.
Effective settings in every group, including all MiniMax H3 options.

Change settings by group, for example `{"minimax_h3": {"render_pass": "two_pass"}}` or the attention options `{"minimax_h3": {"two_pass_use_block_sparse_attention": false, "sage_attention": "auto", "use_memory_efficient_sage_attention": true}}`. Honors If-Match (409 on a stale revision); an invalid value returns 400 SETTINGS_INVALID. Saved under the same keys the Video Builder uses. The project group accepts `use_structured_outputs` and `omit_lyrics_from_video_prompts` (both default false); lyric omission applies to singing with supplied audio only.
Check the saved settings against the chosen video and image modes and report problems before rendering.
Speaking mode only: read project defaults for `silence_before`, `silence_after` (seconds, initially 0) and `fit_duration` (initially true).

Speaking mode only: patch `settings` (`silence_before`, `silence_after`: 0–60 seconds; `fit_duration`: boolean). Reposition scene-owned dialogue and resize/ripple scenes inheriting defaults. Independent music/effect tracks stay fixed. Source files and scene numbering are preserved. Supports If-Match; frozen timelines and running scene renders reject edits.
The saved story layer: idea, arc, brief.
Replace the saved story layer.

Save the Storyboard scene defaults (`defaults`: every key the Builder saves in `builder_storyboard_defaults`, e.g. video style, camera flow, motion speeds, cut frequency, short film planning, temporal and FX settings, plus `story_arc_detail`) and the story fields (`story`: every key of `builder_story_layer`, e.g. `enabled`, idea, strength, world style). Story Mode fields: `story_book_text` replaces the book (parsed into chapters and settings: `Chapter N: title`, then `Setting: name`), `story_settings` (setting looks: a list of `{id, name, look}`, ids as the book gave them), `story_acts` (a list of `{id, chapter_id, title, summary, cast_ids, scene_ids, location_note, direction}`, refused unless every scene is in exactly one act, in order), `story_scene_plan` (a list of `{scene_id, act_id, story_slice, spot, mood, performance_mode, cast_ids, continues_previous, continuation_direction}` with `performance_mode` singing, speaking, no_lip_sync or instrumental; it also sets each scene's performance, maps each planned scene's `cast_ids` onto the scene and makes a scene that continues its predecessor a masked continuation) `story_spot_min_scenes` (1-20), `story_cast_ids` (subject ids the story is about; empty means every card) `story_allow_new_cast` (true lets the story add people with no card) and `story_video_style` (`music_video`, `spoken` or `story_only`: how the story is told on screen).

Write a story step with the project's LLM. `step` is `arc` (from the story idea, lyrics and saved timed Timeline Notes), `brief` or `beats` (a beat per scene without one; `replace_existing`, `scene_ids`, `limit`). Story Mode steps: `book` (the story book from `story_idea` and `tone_notes`; lyrics set mood only), `split` (a story you wrote, sent as `text`, divided into chapters with a setting each, every word kept), `convert` (an older project's song-section story arc becomes the book the same way; the arc is kept), `remove_people` (rewrite the book without the people in `names`, so only the story cast is left; acts and plan are cleared), `chapter` (rewrite `chapter_id` following `direction`), `cast` (story characters with no card yet; nothing saved), `acts` (each chapter gets a run of scenes and is split into acts; `chapter_id` rebuilds one chapter; timed Timeline Notes stay inside one act) and `plan` (each scene of each act gets `story_slice`, `spot` inside the chapter's setting, `mood` and `performance_mode`; `act_id` rebuilds one act; `spot_min_scenes` overrides the saved scenes-per-spot). The plan also writes each scene's performance to the timeline (`performance_mode`, `lyric_no_lip_sync`). `locations` gives each chapter setting a look and each place a location card named `Setting - Spot`, and maps every scene to its spot (`flux_reference_builder.scene_map`); it uses the story and `style_theme` only, never the lyrics. Run it before the acts (no plan yet) and it finds the places inside each chapter setting, the Story Builder's Places tab, keeping the location cards you made by hand. Run it with `map_only: true` after the plan and it asks the LLM nothing: each scene is mapped to the card of its spot, and a card is linked to its setting and acts. `regenerate_looks` rewrites setting looks, `replace_descriptions` rewrites card text (images are never touched). Director, Video and Planning Notes and timed notes win over the story. The book is saved in the story layer as `story_book`, `story_book_text` and `story_settings`; edit the text with PUT /story/settings `story.story_book_text`. Each step also updates the Storyboard Builder's saved copy.
Compact status: scene counts, how many have images, prompts and videos, total duration.

Rebuild or extend the whole timeline from text. `mode` is `durations`, `ranges` or `markers`; `action` is `replace` or `append` (`append_start` sets where appended scenes begin). A line can end with the words for its scene, for example `12.5 --> 16.0 Hello darkness`. On `replace`, when no line carries words, the lyrics of the scenes being replaced move onto the new scenes by time, so they are not lost. Returns `scene_count`, `scenes_with_lyrics` and `lyrics` (`from_text`, `carried_over` or `none`).
Shift all beat markers by `offset_seconds`.
Remove gaps between scenes by moving later scenes earlier.
Merge scenes shorter than `min_scene_seconds` and cut scenes longer than `max_scene_seconds`. `dry_run` shows the plan only. Scenes with rendered video are left alone.

Make the timeline scenes from the lyrics, like Line Mapping: one scene per lyric line, short scenes merged and long ones split to fit `min_scene_seconds` and `max_scene_seconds`. Turns on the lyric lane.

The timed Timeline Notes (the Builder's `+ Timeline Note` markers, saved as `timeline_markers`): `id`, `start` and `end` seconds (`end` is `null` for a point note), `type`, `label`, `note`, and `scene_ids`, the scenes each note overlaps. Story Arc generation uses them as timed story events.
Add a timed Timeline Note. `start` (seconds, required), `end` (later than `start`; leave out or `null` for a point note), `type`, `label`, `note`, optional `id`. The open Video Builder shows it.
Delete a timed Timeline Note.
Change the sent fields of a timed Timeline Note (`start`, `end`, `type`, `label`, `note`). The id never changes; `end: null` makes it a point note.
Snap a scene edge to the nearest beat (`scene_id`, `edge`, `scope`).

The project's transitions in timeline order, as the stitch reads them: `scene_transitions`, each `{id, transition, start, end, seconds, params}` (a block of the timeline like an overlay: `start` and `end` are seconds on the timeline, `seconds` its length), `count`, and `revision`. On a cut between two scenes the block draws one scene into the other, inside a scene it is an effect on that scene's footage. Every stitch draws them, and so do the Video Builder's Render All and Export.

Replace all the project's transitions with `scene_transitions`, a list of `{transition, start, seconds, params, id}`. `transition` is an id from GET /transitions, `start` the time on the timeline in seconds, `seconds` the length 0.1 to 10 (default 0.5), `params` the settings to change from their defaults, `id` optional. Instead of `start`, `after_scene` (the number, 1 = first, or id of the scene before a cut) with `align` (center by default, end or start) puts the block on that cut. Blocks may not overlap: a later one starts where the one before it ends when the video is drawn. The reply is the saved list.

Add one transition, change one, or remove one, and leave the others alone. Without an `id` a new block is added at `start`, or on the cut after `after_scene` (placed around the cut by `align`). With the `id` of an existing block only the fields sent change. A `transition` that is null, empty or `none` removes the block with that `id`, or the blocks that cover the cut after `after_scene`. `seconds` and `params` are as in PUT /projects/{pid}/transitions. The reply is the whole list.
Check the project is consistent: files exist, scene timing, references, settings.
List the project's final videos.
Generate images for many scenes.
Latent chain status for every scene (MiniMax continuity).
Scenes whose latent is out of date because an earlier scene changed.
Rebuild out-of-date latents in order.
Delete MiniMax scratch outputs that are no longer needed.
Index of the MiniMax scratch outputs per scene.
Run the whole build for an existing project (prompts, images, videos, stitch) as one job.
Dry-run plan for the full build: steps, estimated GPU minutes and missing prerequisites.
Apply the project's post-processing settings to every scene video.
Remove the scene's image.
Set the scene image from a file (`source_path`) or upload (`image_data`).
Approve one generated image as the scene's image (`image_path`).
Take the scene image from a frame of a video (`source_video_path`).
Generate a scene image with ComfyUI.
Step through the scene's image history (`index` or `delta`).
Delete a scene's latent (`all`, `reindex`).
One scene's latent file and status.
Apply a LUT to a scene video.
Clear the scene's active video. Files stay on disk.
Match the opening colors of a scene video to the previous scene's last frame.
Recover a MiniMax pass-1 or pass-2 clip from the scratch folder.
Bring back a scene video from a backup or file (`source_path`).

Render one scene's video with ComfyUI (`mode`, e.g. `minimax_h3`). To render against another sound than the project song, send `audio_path` (for example the `no_vocals_path` of POST audio/stems). Trims to the exact timeline length and saves it as `video_NNNN-audio.mp4`. Set `audio_mode: built_in_audio` in the MiniMax settings for H3 voices and sound (all MiniMax video modes and supported passes, including 2 Pass Advanced). With `continuity_mode: latent_continuation_masked` the previous scene must be rendered first (`PREDECESSOR_MISSING` otherwise); it works in Single and 2 Pass. When `continuity_prompt_from_last_frame` is also true, the scene's prompt is first written by the LLM from the previous scene's rendered final frame (the Video Builder's automatic prompt), saved on the scene, and then rendered. A `prompt` in `params` skips that.
Choose which take is the scene's active video (`source_path`).

List the scene's raw (untrimmed) renders, newest first, with length, frame count and whether the file still exists. Takes in a sibling scratch folder with the same project name are marked `other_folder`. Only renders made through the API are always kept: the Video Builder deletes its scratch renders after each render. Use `take` on the trim call.

Trim a scene video as a job. Name the source with `source_path` (default: the scene's current video) or with `take` (`latest` or an index from `video/takes`, the raw render, so the clip can start earlier or end later than the current one). `start` is seconds into the source; give `duration` (and `frames`), or `to_end: true` to end on the source's last frame. Records the new clip on the scene and keeps the old one in its video history.
Make a video from the scene images instead of rendered clips.

Join the scenes' videos into one video (`output_prefix`, default `FINAL_VIDEO`), frame-accurate to the timeline like the Builder's stitch: in a MiniMax H3 project every clip is synced to its scene's frames at 24 fps, so the output has exactly the timeline's frames. `scene_ids` picks scenes by number (1 = first scene) or id and stitches them in timeline order (default: every scene); an unknown scene or a selected scene without a video is a 400. `audio`: `auto` (default) uses the scenes' own audio when every selected MiniMax scene renders with built-in audio, the project song otherwise; `embedded` or `project` forces one. With the project song (or `audio_path`) a selection is cut to its window of the song, so it must be contiguous. `overlays` adds insert clips (`path`, `start`, `end`, `source_start`). The job result lists the stitched `scene_ids`, `audio`, the requested song window (`requested_audio_start`, `requested_audio_duration`; `audio_start` repeats the start) and `expected_frame_count`, and describes the written file from ffprobe: `output_width`, `output_height`, `output_duration` and `audio_duration` (= `output_audio_duration`, the audio actually in the file). An unknown body field is a 400. When the project has overlays (GET /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers), the stitch draws them onto the video and the job result has an `overlay_layers` section (applied, clips, skipped). Send `overlay_layers: false` to leave them out. The project's transitions (GET /projects/{pid}/transitions) are drawn on the video where their blocks lie, and the job result has `transitions` and `transition_notes` when there are any. Send `transitions` (a list of {transition, start, seconds, params}, start on the timeline in seconds) to use other ones for this stitch. The project's filters (GET /projects/{pid}/filters) and effects (GET /projects/{pid}/effects) are drawn on the joined video after the transitions, filters first, and the job result has `looks` and `look_notes` when there are any. Send `filters` or `effects` (a list of {look, start, seconds, intensity, params}) to use other ones for this stitch.
Build the ComfyUI graph for a video `mode` and the given parameters without running it, to inspect what would be sent.
Render many scenes' videos one after another as a GPU job, and stitch them when asked.
Scan the project folder for rendered scene videos and thumbnails and re-link them to scenes.
Summary of the API job queue: running, queued and finished jobs.

Saved RefMods in models/refmods with their type (folder), kind, frame count, tokens and description. Filter with `folder` (for example `identity`). A project switched to the RefMod pipeline (`pipeline: refmod` in the MiniMax H3 settings) renders from these.

Make a saved RefMod from pictures, like RefMods Studio's Create. Needs `name`, `type` (identity, clothing_men, clothing_women, background, generic, object, prop, vehicle or creature) and `paths` (picture files on this computer, one or more, in order). Optional: `crops` (one [x0, y0, x1, y1] or null per picture), `quality` (maximum, high, balanced by default, compact or draft), `mode` (`Full Reference` by default or `Compressed Reference`), `steps` (0 to 2000, default 500), `description` and `overwrite` (replace a RefMod of the same name). A bad request is a 400 with no job. Needs ComfyUI with ComfyUI-MiniMaxH3Mod and the MiniMax H3 video VAE. The job result has `path`, `folder`, `name`, `kind`, `tokens`, `latent_frames` and `canvas`. Then pick the RefMod on a card with PUT references/subjects/{rid}: `source: "refmod"` and `refmod: {"name": "<type>/<name>"}`.

Every MiniMax H3 video setting that can be patched under the `minimax_h3` group: type, default, allowed values and limits. `continuity_mode` takes `latent_continuation_masked` (the previous scene's latent is protected at the start of the next, Single and 2 Pass), `latent_context_frames` takes 39, 90, 141 or 192 for it, and `location_transition_preset` takes `masked`.

The transitions the timeline's transition lane can hold: `transitions` (each with `id`, `origin` (`original` for the app's own, `library` for the gl-transitions collection), `author`, `license`, `description`, `tags` and `params`: name, type, default and range of each setting), and `count`. Use an `id` as `transition` in the project's transitions or in a stitch.
